title: Call Stack
body:
The record of which function called which, maintained by the JS engine. Each call pushes a frame; each return pops it. A thrown error prints the stack as it stood at that moment, which is why a stack trace reads bottom-up as the chain of callers that got you there, and why DevTools' "Sources" panel can show you exactly where execution currently sits when a breakpoint pauses it.

Because [[JavaScript]] is single-threaded, only one stack exists, and it must empty before the [[Event Loop]] can run any queued callback. That is also why asynchronous stack traces used to be nearly useless — the code that scheduled the callback had already unwound off the stack by the time the callback ran. Reading a minified production trace requires [[Source Maps]].
